Rationale.Section: Four notification surfaces were inventoried before design: (1) services/notification — the MarkText-era Fluent toast: a growing blurred circle chasing the cursor (mousemove handler resizing a .fluent div), stack repositioning computed in JS (translate by offsetHeight sums), colors from the separate --notification* token family, click-anywhere-to-confirm semantics; ~70 call sites across store/editor.js (16), store/project.js (11), commands (8+1), editorWithTabs/editor.vue (19), diffView (2), keybindings (3), recent/recentlyClosed (3), searchResultItem/treeFile (2), preferences (2), clipboardOpen (1); (2) components/updateNotice — C-66, the card the owner called the only good-looking one, theme tokens + three buttons + role=status; (3) components/editorWithTabs/notifications.vue — the per-file banner (queue, exclusiveType, confirm action with safe default); (4) components/zoomIndicator — C-49 pill, already clean, untouched by this change. The legacy toast and the update notice also collide geometrically (same corner, z-index 10000 vs 900).

The design was settled interactively with the owner on 2026-10-23; quotes translated from Russian. "Bring everything to a proper design system." "Make the text copyable by default after selection — a developer feature; nobody selects that text unless they need it." "Think and propose what else we missed — maybe keep session notifications." Card variant: shown two live mock variants (severity stripe on the left edge vs severity icon in a tinted circular chip); owner picked the chip: "the icon-chip is cleaner, we take it." Copy confirmation went through three iterations: (a) corner pill "Скопировано" on the card — rejected ("ugly"); (b) selection-anchored green bubble "Скопировано" at the selection end (the iPhone pattern) — rejected ("no caption; just blink somehow — say, blink twice; it's a developer feature, customers don't need it"); (c) final: the selection itself double-pulses green and settles — accepted. History entry point: palette first, bell later. The severity x source model and the agent channel reservation were presented and accepted. The toast/banner/modal boundary was sharpened by the owner ("check that it does not become a substitution of concepts") and is normative in the spec.

The surface test: "if the user stays silent and the card disappears, does a safe state still hold?" Toasts — yes by construction; actions are shortcuts. Banner — yes when a contextual question has a safe default (file-changed-on-disk: ignoring keeps the in-memory version). Modal — no safe default or data risk (unsaved-close). The live audit found the boundary already violated in spirit: showConfirm gave a 10-second toast Promise semantics (resolve on check-click, reject on X, forever-pending on timeout), and both live showConfirm call sites (image-deletion URL copy at editor.js:399, showItemInFolder at editor.js:2120) were actually shortcut actions mis-modeled as confirmations. The genuine question (file changed on disk, editor.js:2268) correctly lives in the banner, and unsavedCloseDialog is a proper modal — no substitution there.

VS Code: status-bar bell + notification center with per-source management and Do Not Disturb — the model for a future bell, explicitly not this change. macOS: notifications group into per-thread stacks (threadIdentifier) with newest-on-top — the dedupKey xN pattern. GitHub Copilot coding agent: a delegated background task is tracked as one live session row that updates in place, not a stream of toasts — the model for future agent events (one live card per agent session). Cursor: agent edits stream into a live diff view, completion is a sound + system notification, and the community actively works around aggressive agent panels — lesson: agent surfaces stay quiet, with only "done" and "needs your decision" allowed to be loud. cmux (a Ghostty-based terminal built around running AI agents): its open UX work is grouping notifications with expandable history — independent confirmation of the grouping pain this design answers.

SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING has no production caller: the IPC routes that fed it were removed in audit-M-1 (bootstrap-ipc.js:373 comment); only its unit test invokes it. The commandExists('pandoc') shim branch and the installPandoc locale key are equally orphaned. The original Electron-era behavior (clicking a check circle that reads as "OK" opens pandoc.org in the browser) was the "sounds like a bug" moment the owner flagged; since no live path reaches it, the fix is deletion, not redesign. The "missing external tool" pattern for any future need: warning card, explicit "Open website" action button — mocked in the same session, recorded here, intentionally not implemented.

An interactive HTML mock (two carousel variants, Paper/Ink switch, live copy-on-select, timer hairline, overflow chip, closing cards) was built on real repo inputs during the 2026-10-23 session: theme token values from paper.theme.css / ink.theme.css (floatBg #FFFDF8 / #20232A, accent #9A6F00 / #FFCF1A, editorColor, inputBg, floatShadow), chromeIcons descriptors (info/warning/error/check/close/message on the 16-grid, 1.4 stroke), and the C-66 button styles. The mock lives outside the repo (session visualization directory, not committed); the spec's R-1 values and metrics are the durable record. The chip variant markup became the normative look; the stripe variant survives only in this design record.

Owner instruction (2026-10-23, translated from Russian): "in the balloon task, change this corner — make sure the export starts working automatically after the rework." Context: C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT (same-day revised draft) ships Word export WITHOUT the pre-export settings modal — one click to the save dialog, remembered options — and its success notification already passes an actions descriptor (a quiet "Export settings" action, source 'export') that today's legacy notify() silently ignores (extra properties are dropped; the degradation is intentional and temporary). Cross-change contract: when this change's notify({ severity, source, actions }) lands, the export success card must render that quiet action with ZERO export-side changes — the same call site upgrades automatically. The quiet style (underlined, editorColor50, R-4) is exactly the "unaccented" button the owner asked for. The action's target: the export-settings surface of the day — the existing exportSettings modal until the dedicated Export settings section exists (backlog item "Export without the settings modal"), the section afterwards. The plan-time CornerMatrix MUST carry this corner, Expected verbatim: "A DOCX export succeeds through the C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT flow; its success card shows the quiet 'Export settings' action; clicking it opens the export-settings surface of the day; the fixture uses the export call site unchanged from before this change (the descriptor was already being passed and silently ignored), proving the upgrade is automatic." Verified in the same 2026-10-23 session: the legacy wrapper accepts title/message/type only (no actions parameter exists to conflict with), so pre-passing the descriptor is forward-compatible, not a hack.

Alternatives.Alternative: Severity stripe on the left edge (mocked, owner-rejected 2026-10-23: "the icon-chip is cleaner"). Kept here as the recorded runner-up in case the chip tint proves weak on a specific theme.
Keep the legacy service and only restyle it: rejected — the JS geometry, mousemove fluent effect and promise semantics are the problem, not just the paint.

Native OS notifications (UNUserNotification / tauri-plugin-notification): rejected for in-app events — they leave the app, cannot offer in-card actions or copy-on-select, and macOS groups them away from the document context.
A notification-center panel with a bell now: deferred per owner ("the palette is the right first step") — palette first, bell only if history proves used.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Title-bar bell + notification-center panel with per-source mute and Do Not Disturb (VS Code pattern) — revisit after the palette history has real usage.

Agent channel events (session card, "needs your decision" sticky, human/agent same-file conflict warning) — implemented when the agent feature itself gets a change bundle; this system reserves the source enum, live-card slot and sticky semantics for it.

Watcher attribution ("changed by agent / another editor / cloud sync" instead of the generic file-changed message) — needs the agent/multi-client integration first; the source channel makes it a message change, not a system change.
Persisting history across sessions — explicitly out; revisit only with a concrete use case.

Scenarios.Scenario: Export succeeds (Word): success card, source label "export", auto-dismiss timer; a quiet underlined "Export settings" action sits under the message and opens the export-settings surface — this action was already present in the export call before the rework and was silently dropped by the legacy toast; after this change it renders with no export-side change.

Export fails (PDF): error card, sticky, full path text selectable; developer selects the path, releases, the selection double-pulses green — the path is on the clipboard; Retry and Details (copy-full-error) actions sit under the message.
Three quick saves plus one export success: three cards max; the oldest collapses into the "More N notifications" chip; clicking the chip opens the palette history with full text and times.
Watcher fires the same project error repeatedly: dedupKey collapses the repeats into one card whose counter climbs (x7); the history keeps each occurrence as its own entry.

Update found: the familiar C-66 message renders as an info card with its three buttons in the shared stack — Update (primary) still installs, Skip still persists; nothing about the update flow changes for the user.
A file changes on disk under the open tab: unchanged behavior — the banner above the document asks; no toast is involved, because ignoring must be safe and visible in context.
A user who never selects notification text sees no new UI at any point: cards, chip, buttons, history only; the copy feature is invisible until a selection exists.
